newsitem.title: GERMANY: Porsche net profit at least 25 mln dmk.
newsitem.headline: Porsche net profit at least 25 mln dmk.

text.p: German sports car maker Dr Ing h.c.F. Porsche AG made a profit in the 1995/96 business year even higher than it had expected, earning at least 25 million marks ($17 million), a Porsche spokesman told Reuters on Tuesday.
Company spokesman Anton Hunger said pre-tax profit would "certainly at least reach 25 million marks."
Porsche, which earned only 2.1 million marks in 1994/95, had previously expected to about double its first half net profit of 10.3 million marks, Chairman Wendelin Wiedeking had said in the spring.
Porsche had already announced sales for the 1995/96 business year which ended July 31 of 2.8 billion marks, up from 2.6 billion marks the year before.
The improved results were due to the undying popularity of Porsche's 30-year old 911 model, the only car the company makes.
Porsche net profit at least 25 million =2
The company will present a detailed accounting of its results in December.
Sales growth has been strongest in the U.S., but weak in Germany where a change in the way company car taxes are treated has hurt demand.
Porsche, which nearly went bankrupt in the early 1990s, had been led back to solid profits by Wiedeking who sharply cut costs and eliminated some models.
The company says it has cut the time it takes to produce one of its Carrera models to 70 hours from 120 hours in 1992/93.
Analysts expect Porsche earnings to continue climbing over the next couple of years.
The company will bring its long-awaited roadster model to market in October and dealers have already received orders for more than 13,000 units, nearly equal to one year's production.

Wiedeking, according to a Porsche spokesman, said last month that the company was talking with its workforce to expand production beyond the stated capacity of around 30,000 units, if demand for the 911 remains strong.
